problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a circuit of six regional warehouses, each situated at precise geographical coordinates:

Warehouse Alpha: (57,163)  
Warehouse Beta: (114,96)  
Warehouse Gamma: (181,172)  
Warehouse Delta: (145,106)  
Warehouse Epsilon: (8,102)  
Warehouse Zeta: (179,145)

Transportation distances between warehouses, measured in kilometers, are predetermined as follows:

Alpha to Gamma: 124.3 km  
Alpha to Delta: 104.8 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 78.2 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 123.3 km  
Beta to Gamma: 101.3 km  
Beta to Delta: 32.6 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 106.2 km  
Beta to Zeta: 81.4 km  
Gamma to Delta: 75.2 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 186.6 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 27.1 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 137.1 km  
Delta to Zeta: 51.7 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 176.3 km

Due to infrastructure limitations, no direct transport link exists between Warehouse Alpha and Warehouse Beta.  
Furthermore, the routing plan must incorporate exactly one of two critical corridors: either the link between Beta and Gamma, or the link between Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total-distance closed circuit that visits each warehouse precisely once before returning to the origin point.
